All 11 tests still pass. Refactoring complete.

## Refactoring Report

**Naming Evaluation (First Priority)**: All function and constant names (`basePremiumsByType`, `basePremiumForItem`, `sumOfItemBasePremiums`, `groupByType`, `basePremiumForGroup`, `basePremium`) clearly reveal their intent. No renames needed.

**Refactoring Applied**: Extracted the inline structural type `{ type: string }`, which appeared 8 times across the file, into a single named `type Item = { type: string }`.

- **Rule 3 (No Duplication)**: The item shape now has one canonical representation instead of being repeated in every signature. When the domain later needs richer items (material, enchantment — visible in the upcoming `it.todo` tests), there is a single place to extend.
- **Rule 2 (Reveals Intent)**: `Item[]` names the domain concept an "insured item" rather than restating an anonymous shape, making signatures read as domain language.

**APP Mass Change**: Runtime mass unchanged (~66) — TypeScript types are erased at runtime, so this is a pure clarity/duplication win with zero mass cost. This is the ideal Rule 2/Rule 3 outcome: better code, no added complexity.

**Rule 4 (Fewest Elements)**: I deliberately did not generalize the block logic further (e.g., a configurable block-count/premium table) — the tests only demand exactly-3-alike → 60, and speculative generalization would add elements the tests don't require.

**Tests**: All 11 passing.
